notes: Time passes at the pace of a conversation now. Play was nudging the story clock four minutes for every turn taken, which meant twenty messages ate the better part of an hour and an evening was gone before anything happened in it. The nudge is measured in seconds instead: a texting exchange moves the clock forty seconds and a scene played out in person a minute, so twenty messages of texting take about seven story minutes rather than forty. That works out at roughly three messages to the minute, which is about how fast people actually text. Jumps are unaffected — a quarter of an hour, an hour, next morning and a picked date all move exactly as much as they say.
